web.title: Who is the oldest person in the world in 2024? | BBC Science Focus ...
web.description: The verifiably oldest ever person in the world is Jeanne Louise Calment, who lived to the age of 122 years and 164 days old.
snippets: The Italian supercentenarian also lived to be 117 years old (plus 137 days) and was born on 29 November 1899 before her death on 15 April 2017. When María Branyas Morera died aged 117 in August 2024 aged 117 years 168 days, she was the eighth-oldest person (with a verifiable age) in history.

120-year-old Jeanne Louise Calment sitting in armchair at home © Ian Cook/Getty Images · Jeanne Louise Calment is the oldest verified person to have ever lived. The Frenchwoman lived to the ripe old age of 122 years and 164 days old.

It’s incredible to imagine what Calment and today's supercentenarians (people who are 110 years old or older) have witnessed in their lifetimes. Just think what it must have been like to be a teenager in the 1920s, to have lived through both World Wars, to have watched the first Moon landings in your fifties or sixties, and then still be alive at the end of the 21st century to observe the latest scientific and technological advances unfold so quickly and dramatically. Today, the oldest person alive (as of August 2025), is the UK's Ethel Caterham.

The UN estimates that the worldwide life expectancy is now 73.3 years – that's about nine years longer than people lived in 1995. The oldest living person as of August 2025 is Ethel Caterham. She is 116 years old.

Since the death of 116-year-old Inah Canabarro Lucas of Brazil on 30 April 2025, 116-year-old Ethel Caterham of the UK is the oldest living person whose age is validated. There are currently 261 validated living supercentenarians by either the Gerontology Research Group (GRG) on the GRG World Supercentenarian Rankings List (WSRL), the Guinness World Records (GWR), or by LongeviQuest (LQ) on their list of oldest living people, whom 231 are female and 30 are male.

web.title: Ranked: The World’s Oldest People in History
web.description: Explore the world’s oldest verified people in history, and see how Jeanne Calment’s 122-year record still stands.
snippets: The longest verified human lifespan belongs to Jeanne Calment of France, who lived 122 years and 164 days, significantly above the other records. Women are the leaders when it comes to extreme longevity, with all 10 oldest recorded people being female, while men’s maximum verified lifespans are several years shorter.

Across cultures and generations, certain individuals have lived well beyond the average human lifespan, offering insights into health, genetics, and lifestyle. In this graphic, we visualize the world’s oldest people in history, highlighting extreme cases of longevity among men and women. The data for this visualization comes from Wikipedia, which compiles verified records from official sources like the Gerontology Research Group or Guinness World Records.

The world’s oldest women have all lived beyond 115 years, with Jeanne Calment of France reaching an incredible 122 years, 164 days. Born in 1875, she witnessed the Eiffel Tower’s construction, both world wars, and the rise of modern technology. She attributed her longevity to a Mediterranean-style life: applying olive oil to her skin, enjoying chocolate and wine, and staying physically active. Third in this ranking is Sarah Knauss, the oldest person ever from the United States.

A slower growth rate does not necessarily indicate a younger population. States such as West Virginia already had among the nation’s oldest populations in 2014, leaving less room for large percentage gains over the following decade.

This is a list of the 100 oldest verified people in world history and list of the 100 oldest verified men in world history. In order to be included on this list, an age claim must have been verified by an international, rather than a national, body. The title of oldest verified person in history belongs to French woman Jeanne Calment (1875–1997) who lived to be 122 years, 164 days, and the title of oldest verified man in history belongs to Japanese Jiroemon Kimura (1897–2013) who lived 116 years, 54 days.

A supercentenarian is considered "verified" if his or her claim has been accepted by an international body that specifically engages in longevity research, such as the Gerontology Research Group (GRG), LongeviQuest (LQ), International Database on Longevity (IDL) or Guinness World Records (GWR).

web.title: Top 10 oldest people in the world: From Jeanne Calment to Kane ...
web.description: Top 10 oldest people in the world: Jeanne Calment of France holds the title of the oldest verified person ever, living an astonishing 122 years and 164 days.
snippets: Some of them were born in the 1800s and went on to see airplanes take flight, astronauts walk on the Moon, and smartphones become part of everyday life. Their lives aren’t just long, they’re windows into centuries of human progress. Take Jeanne Calment of France, for instance. She holds the title of the oldest verified person ever, living an astonishing 122 years and 164 days.

Top 10 oldest people ever lived: For as long as we’ve existed, humans have been curious about one big mystery, why do some people live so much longer than the rest of us? Is it something in their DNA, the way they live, the place they grow up, or maybe just a stroke of luck? While the average person today can expect to live around 73 years, a handful of extraordinary individuals have gone far beyond, not just reaching 100 but pushing past 110 and more.

And while women dominate longevity records, the oldest man ever recorded was also remarkable. Jiroemon Kimura of Japan was born in 1897 and lived to 116 years and 54 days. At the time of his death in 2013, he wasn’t just the oldest man alive—he was the oldest living person in the world.

People who live this long are known as supercentenarians. Of course, proving such extreme ages hasn’t always been easy. In earlier centuries, unreliable or missing birth records meant that many claims of people living past 120 went unverified. Today, however, thanks to rigorous documentation by the Gerontology Research Group (GRG) and Guinness World Records, we have reliable records of the world’s oldest people.
